children: The company will train junior employees to take on selected responsibilities as it targets better utilisation, stable employee costs and improved margins
Tata Elxsi plans to review how work is distributed between senior and junior employees over the next six months as it seeks to improve workforce utilisation, productivity and cost efficiency.

Speaking during the company’s Q2 FY27 earnings call, Manoj Raghavan, Chief Executive Officer and Managing Director, Tata Elxsi, said the company would gradually shift some tasks currently handled by senior employees and technical experts to junior staff. The company has been training junior employees to prepare them for these responsibilities and will track the benefits of the changes over the next six months.

Tata Elxsi’s employee utilisation stood at around 78 per cent during the quarter. Nalin Rana, Chief Financial Officer, Tata Elxsi, said there was scope to improve utilisation, while the company was also reviewing its junior-level hiring.
The company is focusing on workforce planning and employee training to improve productivity while managing employee-related costs as its business grows.
Tata Elxsi implemented salary hikes during Q2 FY27. Rana said improved operational efficiency and lower one-time expenses helped offset the higher employee costs.

He added that salary hikes for the year had been completed and the company expected employee costs to remain largely stable for the rest of the year, apart from selective investments. Operational efficiencies are expected to support margins in the coming quarters as the company continues to focus on cost control.

The company also highlighted strong demand for specialised talent, particularly in engineering research and development (ER&D), as global capability centres (GCCs) continue to expand.Raghavan said retaining talent in this area remained important for the company, even as it works to improve utilisation and productivity across its workforce.

Tata Elxsi reported revenue from operations of Rs 1,055 crore in Q2 FY27, recording growth of 2.3 per cent in constant currency. Management said operational efficiencies and the impact of one-time expenses falling away helped balance the effect of salary increases on margins.
